page: Microsoft Azure M32lds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MDSMediumMemoryv4 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs based on Intel x86_64 processor architecture. Compute resources are coupled with 512 GB of total system RAM, establishing a high memory density of 16 GB per dedicated vCPU. No graphic acceleration hardware is included in this server type.

Storage capabilities include 1,181 GB of bundled local NVMe solid-state disk, designed for high-speed temporary caching, scratch space, and swap operations. In addition to local NVMe capacity, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage, allowing attachment of external persistent block volumes. Network interfaces are provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on private networking or separate gateway assignments.

From an infrastructure perspective, the M32lds_v4 delivers qualitative efficiency for memory-heavy services by avoiding over-provisioning of excess processor cores. A notable operational tradeoff is the ephemeral nature of the integrated local NVMe drive, requiring attached managed disks for persistent data. This machine profile is tailored for large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning backends, high-concurrency caching tiers, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure M32lds_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud virtual machine configured within the MDSMediumMemoryv4 series, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors providing 32 vCPUs alongside 512 GB of memory, delivering a dense allocation of 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 1,181 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and the instance is Premium Storage capable for attached managed disks. The configuration contains zero GPUs. By offering an expansive memory footprint paired with dedicated compute cores and high-throughput local scratch storage, the M32lds_v4 targets enterprise architectures where in-memory capacity is critical. The instance provides cost efficiency for memory-bound systems that do not demand extreme vCPU counts, eliminating the overhead of unneeded compute capacity. Typical enterprise workloads suited for this configuration include large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, high-volume transactional processing engines, and large-scale data analytics caching layers.
